root_cause: In rich 13.8.1 cell highlighting moved to a per-Column `highlight` field (default False), which the renderer reads (render_str(..., highlight=column.highlight), table.py:827). Table.add_column fills it with `highlight if highlight is not None else self.highlight`, but add_row creates missing columns itself with `Column(_index=index)`, which leaves them at False. So `Table(highlight=True, show_header=False).add_row(...)` rendered with no highlighting (issue #3517).
best_solution: In Table.add_row, where a column is auto-created because a row has more cells than the table has columns (`if index == len(columns): column = Column(_index=index)`), pass the table-level setting: `Column(_index=index, highlight=self.highlight)`. That makes the implicit creation path match add_column's default. The statement says it directly: Column.highlight defaults to False, so columns that add_row creates should default to Table.highlight. To find the spot, grep for `Column(` inside add_row.
acceptable_alternatives: Any change that stores highlight == table.highlight on auto-created columns, e.g. routing implicit creation through add_column(), or setting column.highlight = self.highlight after construction. Resolving it only at render time (column.highlight or table.highlight) would not pass, because the test asserts the stored Column attribute.
hidden_test_demands:
tests/test_table.py::test_columns_highlight_added_by_add_row: Table(show_header=False, highlight=True); add_row('1', repr('FOO')); asserts table.columns[0].highlight and columns[1].highlight == table.highlight (the stored attribute), and that Console(record=True).export_text(styles=True) equals exactly '┌───┬───────┐
│ \x1b[1;36m1\x1b[0m │ \x1b[32m'FOO'\x1b[0m │
└───┴───────┘
' (ReprHighlighter styles: bold cyan number, green string).
locating_signals: The title names `table` and `add_row`; the body names `Column.highlight`, `add_row` and `Table.highlight`. `grep -n 'Column(' rich/table.py` inside add_row gives the one line. The function is named outright.
our_outcome_summary: v4, v6 and v7 PASS with a patch byte-identical to gold (529 chars; 55s/29 calls, 41s/12 calls, 45s/21 calls). v8 FAIL with an EMPTY patch after 17s and 14 calls. Its trace shows only the 'locator' role. The first call was malformed (run_skill_script with skill_name stuffed into the file_path string, giving INVALID_ARGUMENTS), then investigate.py failed. The agent found add_row at table.py:423 and read the exact loop with `Column(_index=index)`, then read tests/test_table.py, and the run ended at about 11s without an edit phase or submitted patch. So this was a pipeline/handoff failure, not a wrong fix: the locator stopped with no edit, even though it had already read the one line that needed changing.
generalizable_lesson: (1) When a parent object has a setting that a child also carries (Table.highlight, Column.highlight), find every place the child gets built, including implicit ones like auto-created columns, lazy defaults and factory fallbacks, and pass the parent value along. Grep `ChildClass(` across the module rather than fixing only the explicit add_* API. The fix is usually one kwarg. (2) Harness guard: if a run is about to end with patch_size == 0 after the locator has already read the target snippet, force an edit/submit phase with the located file:line, not a silent exit. An empty patch on a one-line task is a control-flow bug. Validate tool-call arguments too (this run's first call packed two kwargs into one string).
